summary: Los Padres NF lookout on Camuesa Peak built 1935; register says only tower piers remain, while a Peakbagging note citing a USGS datasheet says it was torn down by 1953. Sources disagree.

facts.design: California Region 5 Plan BC-301 cabin on a 10-foot open timber tower
facts.status_note: Register says the tower piers are all that remains; Peakbagging says the lookout was torn down by 1953 per a USGS datasheet and probably nothing is left. Sources disagree
facts.agency: US Forest Service - Los Padres National Forest

access.note: Los Padres National Forest land (register and Peakbagging). A visitor trip report on Hike Los Padres describes a road reaching a turnaround about a quarter mile past the peak. No Forest Service access or closure notice was read, so public access is not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: A visitor's e-bike trip report describes riding the road to a turnaround about a quarter mile past the peak; the report does not mention the lookout site.

events.note: Register says constructed in 1935; Peakbagging photo caption also says built in 1935
Oct 23, 1936 item: during a lightning storm, three lookouts including Camuesa reported a fire near a patrolman; it was the tail light of his car
Peakbagging: torn down by 1953 according to a USGS datasheet (datasheet not read). Register says removal date is unknown

evidence.supports: the lookout is located in Los Padres National Forest
evidence.quote: Located in Los Padres National Forest, Elevation = 3180 ft.

evidence.supports: register says removal date unknown and only the tower piers remain
evidence.quote: Removal date is unknown, the tower piers are all that remains at the site.

corrections.why: Register says the tower piers are all that remains and gives no removal date, so 'gone' overstates what the sources say; Peakbagging's 'nothing left' claim is a conflicting, secondhand note

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register: removal date unknown, tower piers remain. Peakbagging: torn down by 1953 per a USGS datasheet, probably nothing left. Not reconciled; the record is set to ruins and the story reports both accounts.
Register gives 3,153 ft (961 m) for the lookout; Peakbagging gives 3,180 ft. The 961 m figure from the register is used in the record.

sources.title: Camuesa Peak
sources.publisher: Forest Lookouts (volunteer lookout history site), quoting California Ranger

notes_for_editor: Register and Peakbagging disagree on whether anything remains; the USGS datasheet cited by Peakbagging was not read. The 1936 item is secondhand via a volunteer site. Hike Los Padres pages are trip reports from individual visitors, not Forest Service notices; no Forest Service access or closure page was read. Peak elevation on Hike Los Padres (4,180 ft) is the summit, not the lookout. No photos recorded: the Peakbagging photo is credited to Forest Service files but no image URL was read.
